meta.title: Ondra Multimodal Memory
meta.description: Turns what she sees and hears into memories: visual descriptions and speech transcripts are stored as ordinary memories, with the file they came from remembered alongside (handbook §1.5, P1). Three decisions are fixed. First, the memory body exists once, in the memory core; this package only attaches a side table holding modality and source path, and deleting that table breaks no retrieval or injection, only the answer to "which image was this from". Second, entries stay short and the full text is kept: the handbook caps an entry at 200 characters while a three-minute transcript runs to a thousand, so the searchable entry is truncated and the full text lives in the side table. Third, the evidence source follows who actually said it: a transcript is tagged USER because the user spoke those words and whisper is only the channel, while an image description is tagged TOOL because a model produced those words. Getting that backwards either files the user's own words as a model guess, or lets a guess about a picture testify on the user's behalf. Video is composed into two entries as the handbook asks: one from four frame descriptions, one from the audio track. This package registers no tools, runs no timers, makes no network requests and draws no interface: frames belong to the vision plugin, transcription to the speech plugin, the evidence gate to its own plugin, storage to the store plugins, and the interface to the app shell.
